title: [YouPass Collect] - UK Fruit & Vegetable Consumption Trends 2002-2010
prompt: The chart below shows the percentage of the population in the UK who consumed the recommended daily amount of fruit and vegetables in 2002, 2006 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of males, females, and children in the UK who met the recommended daily intake of fruit and vegetables across three separate years: 2002, 2006, and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all three demographic groups experienced an initial increase in consumption levels, peaking in 2006, before declining by the end of the period. Additionally, women consistently recorded the highest percentages throughout, while children remained the lowest across all years surveyed.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding adult populations, in 2002, approximately 25% of women consumed the recommended amount, marginally higher than men, at 22%. By 2006, the female figure had surged to 32%, representing the highest proportion recorded for any group during the entire timeframe, before falling back to roughly 27% in 2010. Men followed a similar trajectory, with their percentage rising to around 28% in the middle year, then declining to 24% in the final year, which was notably close to their starting figure.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for children, their consumption levels started at just 11% in 2002, which was roughly half that of adults. The figure subsequently rose to approximately 16.5% in 2006, marking a 5.5 percentage point increase. However, this upward trend reversed in the following years, with the proportion dropping to roughly 13.5% in 2010, remaining consistently and substantially below both adult categories throughout the entire period.
